options.text: All the statement A, B and C
options.html: All the statement A, B and C

questions.solution:

Nuclear Fission: Nuclear fission is a nuclear reaction in which the nucleus of an atom is bombarded with low-energy neutrons which splits the nucleus into smaller nuclei. An abundant amount of energy is released in this process. Nuclear fission reactions are used in nuclear power reactors since it is easy to control and produces large amounts of energy.

Nuclear fusion: Nuclear fusion is a reaction that occurs when two or more atoms combine together to form to a single heavier nucleus. An enormous amount of energy is released in this process, much greater than the energy released during the nuclear fission reaction.

Fusion occurs in the sun where the atoms of deuterium and tritium combine in a high-pressure atmosphere with extremely high temperatures to produce an output in the form of a neutron and an isotope of Helium.

Perfectly competitive markets are characterized by a large number of sellers and buyers, all producing and consuming homogeneous products. Individual firms in such markets have no control over market prices and face easy entry and exit.


Types of market:

Monopoly:

A monopolistic market is a market formation with the qualities of a pure market. A pure monopoly can only exist when one provider gives a specific service or a product to numerous customers. In a monopolistic market, the imposing business organisation, or the controlling organisation, has the overall control of the entire market, so it sets the supply and price of its goods and services. E.g. Indian Railway.

Oligopoly:

An oligopoly is a market form with a few firms, none of which can hold the others back from having a critical impact. The fixation or concentration proportion estimates the piece of the market share of the biggest firms. E.g - commercial air travel.
